core_obligations: Note that the sufficiency direction is immediate: the two displayed families of relations compute the sum of the m_j tensor y_j as zero (proof line 26261).
For the converse, present N as the quotient of a direct sum of copies of R by a kernel K and tensor the short exact sequence with M (proof lines 26263-26271).
Use that the given element lies in the image of K tensor M to write it as a sum of k_i tensor x_i, and read the coefficients a_{i,j} off the components of the k_i (proof lines 26272-26274).
proof_roadmap: Get one direction from the two displayed relations (proof lines 26260-26261).
For the other, tensor a presentation of N with M and lift the element through the presentation (proof lines 26262-26275).
difficulty_reason: The lemma rewrites the vanishing of a finite tensor sum, along chosen generating sets of M and N, as the existence of a coefficient matrix satisfying two systems of relations (statement lines 26239-26258). The proof does not work with the universal property of the tensor product directly: it presents N as a quotient of a direct sum of copies of the ring by a kernel K, tensors the presentation with M using right exactness, lifts the given element to K tensor M, and then reads the entries of the lifted elements as the required coefficients (proof lines 26260-26275). Deciding to present N and then lift is the substance, and the author records both systems of relations exactly as they come out. H2.
